action.about: Something a user runs on an object: a menu row, a palette entry or a key. A surface places it by id.

block.about: A copyable block (code, a command, a log, a file excerpt): Copy, Send to terminal and Add to composer derive from it.

condition.about: A simulated real-life state (a slow link, a usage limit, a huge diff): one simulator induces it, a stage puts the app into it, one measure says whether it holds, and every surface its walks visit needs a case.

scaffold.entry:
export const {{name}} = define.condition({
	id: "{{id}}",
	group: "real-life",
	said: { date: "{{date}}", quote: "{{said}}", where: "{{where}}" },
	appliesTo: { walks: "all", categories: [] },
	simulator: "unbuilt",
	profile: {},
	measure: [],
	verdict: "reviewed",
	ci: { debt: "climb" },
	status: "parked",
});

lens.about: A holistic review angle (security, CI cost, test honesty, settings defaults): it groups conditions or names a check, and carries the reviewer's rubric. It has no pass/fail of its own.

setting.about: A setting: its page and anchor, its name and sentence for search, its stored key, and the surfaces it shapes.

surface.about: An object on screen with menus: right-click, its ⋯ and the palette list the actions it places. Rendered as <Surface id>.

fields.rubric: Look at each feature from another feature's side: what it should link to, count, filter by or tell, and where a surface stands alone with no way in or out.

said.quote: do you understand how CI is killing me and why I don't want lanes to keep trying to fix it
said.where: operator, organizer session, 2026-11-10 17:45Z; also 2026-11-11 15:44Z and 15:50Z, recorded-agent CI cases and no real limit hits

check.measure: median job minutes per workflow over the last 3 runs, and CI using fake agents only
check.budget: ratchet rows measure/ci-minutes: they only fall

fields.rubric: Per-PR CI runs only the cells the diff touches, nightly runs the rest, and CI spends no real tokens: fake agents only.

said.quote: what was the verdict about our tests lying? Are we good there?

check.measure: hits of the three test rules (bare assertion, expect inside a branch or mock, early return), tests that match nothing, mutation score, and retyped thresholds
check.budget: ratchet rows tests.lint and measure/*: they only fall

fields.rubric: A test asserts every claim in its name, the exact value the behaviour produces, and fails when it cannot set up its condition. A passing run with no tests matched is a failure.

said.quote: I want to do and build a comparable app, we first get a good enough app out and then worry about the small small security details

check.measure: simulated attacks failing, high advisories (with dependency-audit.yml) and open findings that are cheap, serious and reachable

fields.rubric: Fix now only a finding that is reachable without effort, does real harm and has a small fix; every other one goes to the one security backlog issue.

said.quote: each integration point that we add is more technical debt that we have to maintain

fields.rubric: Parked. An integration is cheap to add, update and remove, and a break shows up as a disabled integration, not as silence.

said.quote: game-feel without gamification
said.where: organizer relay of the operator, 2026-11-04 (ui-reset PROMPT.md); verbatim unconfirmed

fields.rubric: Parked. Ease and flow: a first win in under a minute, instant feedback, one obvious next step. No streaks, points, badges or leaderboards.

said.quote: Why do all our texts and icons look jagged and not production grade?

fields.rubric: Look at DPR-2 shots at 1600 px and at phone width: text, icons and borders are crisp and look production grade. A 1x shot proves nothing.

said.quote: we somehow need a way to know when multiple surfaces are shown on a screen then how many of them show duplicate info. That just clutters up the UI.
said.where: operator, #1101 - Wave 2: thread UX hill climb, round 2, Operator review 2026-11-15

check.measure: facts (registry/closed/fact.ts) about one thread shown in more than one place on an evidence screen, less the declared repeats
check.budget: the measure/facts row in registry.ratchet.tsv, which only falls

fields.rubric: Each fact (agent, model, host, status, cause, a time) shows in one region of a screen, the one where it lives best. A second showing is declared in the fact's entry with its reason, or removed. The transcript's own words never move.

said.quote: having good default settings and adding controls in settings section

fields.rubric: Every setting ships with a default that works without opening Settings, a control, and a one-line description; a feature that adds behaviour adds its setting in the same change.

said.quote: what about clearing things up automatically when a thread is settled or marked done
said.where: operator, organizer session, 2026-11-11 08:40Z; also 2026-11-10 10:12Z, many node.exe left running

fields.rubric: Settling or finishing a thread ends everything it started: watches, crons, worktrees, child threads and processes. Look for what is still running afterwards.

said.quote: threads are flat, independent siblings, with no parent tree and no grouping in the sidebar
said.where: operator, standing decision on #1101 - Wave 2: thread UX hill climb, round 2

check.measure: thread rows or Home cards inside another row, a fold, a group or a starter's count

fields.rubric: Every thread is its own row in the sidebar, Needs you and Home. Who started it is a mark on the row, never a container, chevron or count. Many agent-started rows are sunk or filtered, not folded.

said.quote: the lens of token usage tracking for performance tracking and improvements
said.where: operator, organizer session, 2026-11-11 08:46Z; also 2026-11-12 15:43Z on inference cost, and 2026-11-13 07:17Z on notification cost

fields.rubric: Token and cost use is visible and recorded per turn; polish and notifications are weighed against the inference and attention they cost.

9.3.text: Rows collapse by default and expand to input and result; a running row says what it is doing; a failed row says why in one line

9.4.text: A turn that edited files ends with an "N changed files +a −b" card linking to the diff

9.5.text: A long group shows its ends and folds the middle; a flagged or asked step is never hidden

10.1.text: In-session sub-agents are collapsed nodes in the transcript, never rows in the list

10.2.text: An agent-started thread carries a started-by mark linking to its starter, and the starter shows a "Started thread X" row linking to it

10.3.text: A message between threads is a labelled card: sender's title as a link, time, text that expands; sent and received read differently

10.4.text: A message reaches a running thread at its next pause and reopens an idle one; a settled thread keeps it unread; the sender sees which; a steer delivers now

10.5.text: Starting obeys Settings (ask, allow, never; caps; daily budget); a message loop stops at the pair cap with a visible notice

11.1.text: A context meter is always visible: used / size, a warning tone before compaction, and the compaction point

11.2.text: /context lists what fills the window by category, with tokens and percent, and names the largest items

11.3.text: Compaction is a labelled divider with tokens before and after; a failed one offers Retry; a focus instruction is echoed

11.4.text: Cache state (warm until, or cold) is stated plainly

11.5.text: One composer control toggles "Compact N" and "Keep N", and its hover says what the next send does

12.1.text: A thread of any length opens within one round trip at the unread mark, a linked item or the tail; pages load around a seq with a per-page budget

12.2.text: Rendering is windowed: DOM bounded at 5,000+ items, scroll holds on prepend, "Scroll to end" and an "N new" pill when scrolled away

12.3.text: A cached snapshot of the last-seen window renders first, then reconciles

12.4.text: The live stream resumes from a cursor and replays only the gap; a dropped connection shows a reconnect line, never a reload

12.5.text: A failed page shows Retry in place; a folded turn does not need its contents loaded

12.6.text: Folding follows the content's purpose, the view level (Focus, Standard, Full) is saved and keyed, and unfolding keeps the reader's place

13.1.text: Ctrl/Cmd+F opens our find bar at the transcript's top right; a second press selects the query; Escape closes it and returns focus to the composer

13.2.text: The count covers the whole thread ("25/26"), says when it is still counting, and shows "0/0" for no match

13.3.text: Enter / Shift+Enter, F3 / Shift+F3 and the chevrons move between hits; each scrolls into view, loading its page, highlighted in place, the active one distinct

13.4.text: It works on a windowed 5,000-item thread with no full download; a failed search shows Retry

13.5.text: Scope chips (All, Mine, Agent, Tools) and a case toggle; the palette finds message text across threads and opens find at the hit

13.6.text: On a phone, the thread menu opens find above the keyboard

14.1.text: The rail sits at the far left of the thread pane, one dash per exchange, its hover card never covering the message being read

14.2.text: Hover or focus opens a card (prompt's first words bold, the final message clamped to 3 lines); click or Enter jumps there, even into an unloaded part

14.3.text: A break gets its own dash in order, coloured by kind; a run of one break is one dash; its card names the break and its time

14.4.text: A long thread shows a window of about 15 dashes around the current position, ends fading

14.5.text: Find hits mark dashes only while find is open, the active hit brightest

14.6.text: Arrows, Home and End move the card; F and Shift+F jump between failures; one screen-reader jump link per dash; a phone shows no rail

15.1.text: A thread's PR is one header chip and one panel row showing title, number, branch pair, tone word, N/M checks, review verdict and merge state

15.2.text: Checks expand to each run with its state and log link; a failing run sorts first and shows its failing step or a log tail

15.3.text: A failing check or open review thread has one action drafting an editable message with the check name, a log excerpt and the head SHA

15.4.text: Review threads show path:line, author, resolved state and an excerpt, and jump to the line in the diff

15.5.text: The watch state is visible and changeable; each pushed status is a quiet transcript line; the row updates without a reload

15.6.text: The row says which incident, report and cause the PR answers

15.7.text: A PR's checks are found in two clicks from a cold thread

16.1.text: One diff surface: a file tree with a filter and per-file +/−, split and unified (unified when narrow), a wrap toggle and expandable context

16.2.text: Scopes all vs base, this turn and uncommitted, with the active scope named

16.3.text: A + on a line opens a comment; several batch into one message with path, line and quoted line, shown as composer chips

16.4.text: Per-file and per-hunk revert, each confirmed and undoable; a per-turn Undo sits on the transcript row

16.5.text: Open a file in place with its line highlighted or in the editor at that line; copy its path or attach it as context

16.6.text: A file named in the transcript opens at its line in one click; the user's edits are told apart from the agent's

16.7.text: A huge diff on the slow link: tree and +/− within one round trip, patches per file on demand, groups foldable, no main-thread task over 200 ms

17.1.text: A Usage view: range chips, project and agent scope, Tokens and Cost tabs, a daily chart, a Model / Day breakdown; cost labelled an estimate, an unpriced model says so

17.2.text: A model row opens a card: cost, tokens, cache hit rate, cost per million tokens

17.3.text: A Limits tab shows each agent's windows as "N% left" with reset chips and a pace tick; an agent that reports none says so

17.4.text: The dock names the limit hit, the resume time in local time and what happens next, offers "Switch agent or model"; an unknown reset says so with "try N of 5"

17.5.text: A limit hit while away raises a notification with the reset time, and the row shows the same time

17.6.text: A mid-turn limit keeps the partial transcript and pauses the turn (not failed); a restart keeps the reset time and queue, nothing resumes twice

17.7.text: API-key failures are classified by status and code first; each mode (out of credit, 429, rejected key, spend cap, overloaded) has its own words, action and resume rule

17.8.text: The limit dock is one slim strip above the composer ("Usage limit reached · Resumes …") with Cancel auto-resume and Snooze until reset; the row carries a Limited badge

17.9.text: Every incoming message and provider call keeps its own outcome row with its time; a limit never fails the thread or drops a message; messages queue and deliver once

18.1.text: Search across Settings; each row is a name, one sentence and a control; a changed row shows Reset

18.2.text: Pages: Models (a default per use), Permissions (ladder, per-agent default, alert-run ask policy), Agent-started threads (caps), Agents, Appearance, Notifications, Keyboard shortcuts

18.3.text: Advanced options are folded inside each group

18.4.text: A dangerous choice states its risk at the row and asks for a second confirmation

18.5.text: The composer's pickers match the Settings defaults

18.6.text: A host-only row says so and is read-only from a paired device

18.7.text: Every Settings page is reachable on a phone

19.1.text: One overlay for threads, incidents, alerts, projects, schedules and actions, with type tabs and recents when empty

19.2.text: The hovered result previews its status, last line, PR and limit

19.3.text: A key opens row actions (open in panel, Settle, copy link), and the footer lists the keys

19.4.text: Every action is reachable, and message text across threads is found

20.1.text: One overflow menu with the same items in the header and the row, and the keys shown

20.2.text: Items: Rename, Pin, Fork here, Side question, Settle, Archive, Work in / Move to worktree, Copy link or transcript

20.3.text: A disabled item says why; a destructive item confirms or offers Undo

21.1.text: A new-tab page lists every tool with its key

21.2.text: Panes tile, and an unavailable pane says why and what to do

21.3.text: The browser keeps a persistent profile, and the agent can drive it

21.4.text: The files pane opens at the path an agent message cites

21.5.text: The right panel resizes from its border, a button widens it over the main column, and the width is kept per person

21.6.text: On wide screens the thread's top-right box is always present at a fixed place and size, giving way to the open panel

22.1.text: A list of scheduled tasks with state, cadence, next run and last result

22.2.text: Each scheduled run is a thread with unread state

22.4.text: Templates: watch a service, a daily digest, re-check a PR

22.5.text: A scheduled run that hits a limit shows it on its card, with the reset

23.1.text: Each failure sentence names the cause and one next action, with a button

23.2.text: A lost connection is a quiet dock, not a modal, and the draft is kept

23.3.text: After a restart each interrupted run reads "Interrupted by restart" with Resume, and a limit keeps its reset time

23.4.text: No raw error codes are shown

23.5.text: A failed turn is one quiet red line with its cause, not a card

sidebar.row.title: A thread's row in the sidebar

home.card.title: A card or row on Home and Needs you

list.row.title: A row on a list page: What changed, the board, Services

incident.card.title: An alert thread's summary card above the transcript

strip.title: A status strip over the box (limit, blocked, failed)

composer.title: The message box and its pickers

fixture-text.text: Thread titles, replies and file contents are seeded fixtures or fake agents replaying recorded sessions. Don't score their wording, only the product's own words.

said.quote: notes for known false alarms: fixture text, phone chips scroll by design, ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES = browser under load

phone-chips-scroll.text: At 390 px the chip rows scroll sideways inside their own strip on purpose; the page itself must not scroll sideways (measures.md counts that).

said.quote: notes for known false alarms: fixture text, phone chips scroll by design, ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES = browser under load

browser-under-load.text: ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES and 'Failed to fetch dynamically imported module' come from a browser under load on the shared machine, not from the app; reload once and note it.

said.quote: notes for known false alarms: fixture text, phone chips scroll by design, ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES = browser under load

away-once.text: The away view opens on the first visible tab after a long absence, once; a later visit, or another judge's visit first, finds it spent. Its shot is in the evidence folder.

said.quote: only first visit after being away shows it, so 768/390 Home shots lack it

shared-server.text: Drafts follow the operator across devices by design: on a server shared with another judge, Home's draft changes under you. Each judge runs on their own sim; a thread's state changing under you means another walk on the same thread, so use another thread of the same kind and note it.

said.quote: judges sharing a server wrote into each other's Home draft

server-clock-ahead.text: host.standby proves itself by skipping the server's clock 11 minutes, as a laptop's sleep does, so on a sim a time near now can read a few minutes in the future ("in 2m"). Score the time format, not that offset.

said.quote: Watch the rollout ... in 2m (Events, a simulated PrismaLens after its standby skip)

app.title: PrismaLens hit a problem
app.line: Your threads and drafts are kept, and running agents keep going. Reload to carry on.

page.title: This page stopped working
page.line: Nothing you saved is lost. Reload the page, or go home.

thread.title: This thread stopped showing
thread.line: The thread is kept and its agent keeps running. Reload it, or go home.

transcript.title: The transcript stopped showing
transcript.line: The agent and the box below still work.

panel.title: This panel stopped showing
panel.line: The rest of the thread still works.

prose.why: Narration between steps; the turn's last words and the last before an ask or stop are read.

ask.why: An ask waits on you: never hidden.

line.why: A notice the run said once.

level.why: A call the run's level answered without asking.

finding.why: Evidence or a suspect recorded mid-turn.

operator.why: Your message: folds past about 6 lines. The note PrismaLens sends on Resume is work: one restart line until opened.

end.why: How the run ended: report, stop or limit.

node.why: An event a lane draws; its own class comes from EVENT_FOLD.

inbound.why: A message from another thread or source: its sender and 3 lines.

outcome.why: What became of a call you approved or denied.

merge.title: Merge rule
merge.text: A category's score is the median of the three judges (Codex, Opus and agy), after calibration. Every flaw below 8.5 that a judge backs with a screenshot goes on the fix list, whatever the median. A cell without a valid stamp is not tested: its categories are null.

said.quote: three judges score each checkpoint from the same prompt: Codex, Opus and agy

stop.title: Stop rule
stop.text: The bar is met only when every category is at 8.5 or above on two checkpoints in a row.

said.quote: three judges score each checkpoint from the same prompt: Codex, Opus and agy

words.focus: Your messages, each turn's summary and its answer
words.standard: Working steps fold; answers, asks and notices stay open

words.sent: This message and later ones stay unread: these two threads reached today's message cap
words.received: This message woke nothing: these two threads reached today's message cap

resumed.why: 'Resumed in the same session' joins the next message's meta.

responseActions.why: Copy and Fork stay in view on the latest response; earlier ones show on hover or focus.

you.why: Your own message: the bubble says who.

thread.why: Another thread or agent wrote it.

trigger.why: An alert, schedule or webhook sent it.

bare.title: The app with no condition applied, and one thread with helpers

seeds.live: the thread Send two helpers, whose agent's in-session helpers show as collapsed nodes

ci.title: The conditions that have a CI case

all.title: Every active condition, and the 5,000-item thread

seeds.live: the thread with 5,000 items (Ctrl+F, the rail, scrolling back), and a starter with 39 threads it started
the thread Send two helpers, whose agent's in-session helpers show as collapsed nodes

api.low-disk.title: The API told its disk is nearly full: statfs reports 20 MB and git worktree add fails
api.low-disk.run: pnpm sim up --only git.worktree-disk (the API loads the low-disk stub)

clock.standby.title: The API's wall clock jumps past a wake while its timers did not run, as after a laptop sleeps
clock.standby.run: pnpm sim up --only host.standby, then its Skip button on the sheet

fake.budget-cap.title: A scripted agent whose spend climbs to $5, then hits the organization spend cap

fake.protocol-drift.title: A scripted agent a protocol version ahead, sending update kinds the host does not know

fake.runaway.title: A scripted agent repeating the same call ten times a second until stopped

fake.settle-cleanup.title: A thread holding a wake, a cron, a worktree and a running process, then settled

fake.usage-telemetry.title: A scripted agent that reports usage on every turn

git.fixture.title: A project thread's worktree put into a git state: a conflict, a force-push or a deleted branch

pw.time-zone.title: A browser in Asia/Kolkata with the en-IN locale

pw.two-devices.title: The same running thread on a desk and a 390 px phone; the phone steers mid-turn

fake.failure-case.title: A recorded provider failure played against a running PrismaLens

fake.message-loop.title: Two scripted threads that message each other in a loop

host.restart.title: Two threads mid-turn, then the server restarts under them with Resume after a restart off
host.restart.run: pnpm sim up --only host.restart (it restarts the server through pnpm sim restart)

net.throttle.title: A throttling proxy for any browser or the phone, which stamps what it saw

pw.judge-evidence.title: The design matrix shot through the slow link at desk and phone widths, measured per screen

seed.huge-diff.title: A seeded thread that replays feat/w2-cp against main, measured on the slow link with a 4x CPU

seed.huge-output.title: Threads seeded with a huge log in a reply, a huge folded paste and a huge binary file

seed.away.title: A night away: the operator left 9 hours ago, and threads finished, failed, hit a limit, got blocked and asked meanwhile

seed.thread-list.title: 40 flat threads in every status, 12 of them started by agents, with asks waiting in several

unbuilt.title: No simulator chosen yet: a parked entry from intake

out_of_credit.name: Out of credit
out_of_credit.head: Out of credit
out_of_credit.next: Nothing happens by itself. Add credit, then Try again. Your draft is kept.

key_rejected.name: API key rejected
key_rejected.head: API key rejected
key_rejected.next: Nothing happens by itself. Update the key in the agent's settings, then Try again. Your draft is kept.

spend_cap.name: Spend cap reached
spend_cap.head: Spend cap reached
spend_cap.next: PrismaLens can't change this cap. Raise it on the provider's account, then send your message again. Your draft is kept.

disk_full.name: No disk space left for its worktree
disk_full.head: No disk space left for its worktree
disk_full.next: Nothing happens by itself. Free space by removing old workspaces, then send your message again. Your draft is kept.

auto_critical.why: A critical alert fired; runs start on their own for those

auto_tier.why: The service's tier starts a run on its own when an alert fires

re_trigger.why: The alert fired again after the incident ended

quote-new-thread.title: Quote a selection into a new thread

answer-ask.title: Answer an ask from the dock

agent-starts-thread.title: An agent starts a sibling thread, messages it, and the sibling finishes

restart-resume.title: A thread restarted mid-run reads Interrupted, offers Resume, and resumes once

said.quote: organizer, checkpoint 4 order, from the operator's Interrupted/Blocked and huge-diff requirements

blocked-fix.title: Blocked by a full disk and by a rejected key, each offering its own fix from the thread, the row and Home

said.quote: organizer, checkpoint 4 order, from the operator's Interrupted/Blocked and huge-diff requirements

review-huge-diff.title: Review a huge diff (about 870 files): the tree before any patch, lazy patches, folding, group filters, no freeze
